newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ's Sherwin says nothing new in Brash comments.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ's Sherwin says nothing new in Brash comments.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Deputy Governor Murray Sherwin said on Friday there was nothing new in comments attributed to Governor Don Brash on the level of the New Zealand dollar.

Sherwin said the reported comments on the New Zealand dollar being "overvalued" were no different from those made by Brash in a post-election briefing last year, based on a 30-year average for the currency.
"It moves in cycles, and right now it looks as if it's running to the top of one of its cycles," Sherwin told Reuters.

Sherwin confirmed that Brash, speaking on Thursday in Sydney, had also reiterated his familiar theme that the bank, if it could control the mix of monetary conditions, would prefer a lower exchange rate and higher domestic interest rates.

"What he said was no different from anything he's said here for some months," Sherwin said, adding there was nothing in the comments that departed from the bank's line in its December Monetary Policy Statement or the post-election briefing.
The New Zealand dollar opened at US$0.6907/14 and 67.91 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6930/37 and 68.22 at Thursday's close. Brash's comments in Sydney were reported overnight.
By 11.25 a.m. (2225 GMT), the Kiwi was trading at 0.6912/19 and 67.96 on the TWI.
